title: Sister of man shot by police seeks public help
article: The sister of a man shot and killed by Vancouver police in the Downtown Eastside on Boxing Day is hoping people will open their hearts and help bring her brother's body home to Prince Rupert.
"I'm trying to get the message out that we have lost a family member," said Teresa Chenery. "We wanted to ask the community for donations to bring him home for burial."

The body of Gerald Samuel Chenery, 29, remains in the morgue at Vancouver General Hospital while Teresa, his closest living relative, tries to find a way to have his remains properly looked after. She is on income assistance and supports six children.
"His body can be released, but we don't have the income \[to bury him\]," she said.
"Income assistance said they used to help with bereavement costs, but with all the cutbacks in funding they are no longer under any obligation to help me."
The bother and sister were adopted by an RCMP officer and left Prince Rupert when they were children.
"Gerald was adopted by Sergeant J.W. Chenery," said Teresa Chenery. "Later, he contacted my original family that adopted me, so I could move in with my brother."
The pair lived with the sergeant for most of their lives in Lillooet.
Teresa had her children there, but later returned to Prince Rupert, where she now lives. Gerald left Lillooet when he was a teenager.
Although her brother had been in trouble with the law in the past, she is unsure what could have led to the police shooting.
"I talked to my brother on Dec. 23," said Chenery. "He said he was just released from jail and I said 'Good, when are you coming home?'
"He wanted to be reunited with his family, stay out of trouble and help me raise my kids."
The siblings had spoken about land owned by their biological father in Kincolith and the possibility of living in a house together there.

"The last thing he said to me was 'We'll be together sooner than you think,'" said Chenery, choking back tears. "Next time I heard about it, two policemen came to my door \[Dec. 27\] and took me outside.
"Local RCMP told me my brother was shot to death by Vancouver police and they couldn't give me any information."

What police will reveal is that two officers were conducting a patrol at around 9:30 p.m. Boxing Day when they came upon a man in the south lane of the 200 block of East Hastings Street. A police check revealed Gerald Chenery was wanted on a Canada-wide warrant after his parole had been revoked for failing to report to his halfway house after being released from jail.

When the officers attempted to arrest the man, who had previous offences including ones involving a weapon, he pulled a knife on them, said Vancouver police spokeswoman Const. Sarah Bloor. She said he ignored repeated requests to drop the knife, and lunged at one of the officers, cutting one of them on the hand.
